mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals labor market weakness, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns as consumer spending and corporate earnings could decline.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 40% of cases when UNRATE increases, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 4.5%, it indicates monetary tightening, which could lead to negative S&P 500 returns as borrowing costs increase and investment decreases.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 35% of cases when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: If GDP (GDPC1) growth accelerates while housing starts (HOUST) decelerate, it may indicate an imbalance in demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns as economic growth falters.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 30% of cases when GDPC1 and HOUST diverge, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) signals strong supply-side activity, which may lead to positive S&P 500 returns as production and economic activity expand.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of cases when INDPRO increases, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) signals a strong labor market, which may lead to positive S&P 500 returns as consumer spending and corporate earnings increase.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 35% of cases when PAYEMS > 200k, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals monetary easing, which may lead to positive S&P 500 returns as borrowing costs decrease and investment increases.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 30% of cases when FEDFUNDS < 3%, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: If retail sales (RSAFS) increase while consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) decreases, it may indicate deflationary pressures, leading to negative S&P 500 returns as profit margins could decline.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 25% of cases when RSAFS and CPIAUCSL diverge, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals monetary tightening, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns as borrowing costs increase and investment decreases.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 35% of cases when FEDFUNDS increases by >0.5%, this hypothesis is rejected.
